name: signal-resolve
title: Signal Resolve
desc: Noisy scope traces resolve to a clean line and the logo with Less noise. More signal.

name: signup-flow
title: UI Signup Flow
desc: A signup card composition: a real shadcn-style card (header, labeled Full Name / Email / Password / Confirm fields, primary + Google-outline buttons, sign-in footer) whose cursor fills each field top-to-bottom, then clicks Create account (hover → press → loading → success) as a success toast slides in. A pure orchestrator — every channel comes from a composed primitive's transition hook.

name: simulated-cursor
title: Simulated Cursor
desc: Animated mouse cursor moving between waypoints with click ripple feedback.

name: single-stroke
title: Single Stroke
desc: A giant 27 drawn in single strokes sits beside a coral 'Mar' panel and a demo-day line.

name: skeleton
title: UI Skeleton
desc: A skeleton→content crossfade whose loading/loaded state is a pure function of the timeline. The Skeleton renderer is pure (reads no frame); only the composed SkeletonBlock shimmer reads it. SkeletonStyle opacities sum to 1 so the box never dims; real children sit in normal flow and the placeholder (a lines/card layout or a custom node) is an absolute overlay.

name: skeleton-block
title: UI Skeleton Block
desc: A shimmer placeholder block — a motion atom (spinner pattern). A directional highlight gradient sweeps across deterministically from useCurrentFrame() and loops seamlessly. Configurable width/height/radius/speed and base/highlight colors.

name: slash-wipe
title: Slash Wipe
desc: A gradient slash wipes across and reveals a large title, '/transitions', with a one-line sub.

name: slide-doors
title: Slide Doors
desc: Two panels slide apart like doors to reveal 'Arriving in your repo.' with an accent word.

name: slide-swap
title: Slide Swap
desc: A scene sequencer where the outgoing content is shoved off on an accelerating curve and the next springs in from the opposite edge, on one canvas, with no overlap.

name: slider
title: UI Slider
desc: A slider whose fill is a numeric value channel plus a thumb idle/hover/press channel (dual-channel value-channel deviation). The Slider renderer is pure (clamped 0–100 value, thumb scale, grab-ring opacity); useSliderTransition reads the frame and eases both channels — value as a numeric lerp, the thumb visual from its state presets. Muted track + primary range + bordered thumb with a derived grab ring.

name: slim-count
title: Slim Count

name: slit-reveal

name: slit-scan

name: slope-chart

name: slot-machine-roll

name: smash-count

name: smoke-dissolve

name: snap-click

title: Agent Steps
desc: AI agent steps animation: a streaming task log with spinner and checkmarks for agent demos. An agent narrating its own work: the prompt lands in a pill, and under it a log writes itself one line at a time — each step running with a faint spinning globe, then flipping to past tense behind a check while the whole column steps up a row so the live line always sits on the centre. When the work is done the column swells and clears, and the last line slides to the middle and becomes the answer. Every

name: announce-title
title: Announce Title
desc: Launch title animation, product announcement intro with kinetic typography. A four-shot launch title: the eyebrow rushes past the camera on a receding type plane and lands on a colour field, the name assembles word by word on paper, and a macro pan across the tagline cuts wide as the line builds itself last word first while a white sweep drains it out of colour. Content, palette and the mark that leads the closing line are all props.

name: answer-highlight
title: Answer Highlight
desc: AI answer highlight animation, ChatGPT-style chat response with a text selection. A question in a pill, an answer that writes itself a word at a time, and then the beat the whole shot is for: a caret lands mid-sentence and a selection band drags across one statement, wrapping the line the way a real one does — and settles onto the single word that matters. Name the sentence and the word as strings; the run is found in the answer for you, punctuation and all.

name: answer-stream
title: Answer Stream
desc: Streaming AI response animation, from the send button to the answer typing in. The beat after send: a macro shot on the button that cuts — hard, on its fastest frame — to the answer building itself on the page, while the camera pulls back 1.364× about a focal point above the frame to keep up with it. Every word arrives hot and cools to the foreground.

name: block-wordmark
title: Block Wordmark
desc: Logo sting and wordmark animation: blocks build into your brand name. A wordmark builds out of solid blocks — a square scales in, a coloured deck fans out around it and winds back, the stack collapses and stretches into one block per letter, then each block flashes a colour and swaps for its real letterform.

name: bloom-lockup
title: Bloom Lockup
desc: Logo reveal in four seconds. A wall of finished work blooms outward from your logo, cuts in tight on it, then bends away through a lens and a flash while the logo rises to take its wordmark and tagline. Measured frame by frame off a reference recording.

name: button-press
title: Button Press
desc: Cursor clicks a button: a cursor walks onto a split action button (label, divider, chevron), it darkens on hover, gives on press, spins while pending and lands on a drawn tick. The deploy, publish or send beat of every launch video. Built on cursor-track.

name: capture-reveal
title: Capture Reveal
desc: Screenshot capture animation: a toast counts "Capturing selection…" up to 100% over a browser window, the window drops away and shrinks, the toast pops to "Copied to clipboard." and a two-line headline rises out from behind the window while the cursor glides up. Every curve was measured off a recording frame by frame: the window's drop and shrink share one cubic-bezier, the toast pops on another, the headline rises without scaling or blurring, and type moves by fractions of a pixel.

name: card-rail
title: Card Rail
desc: Card carousel animation: cards flicked sideways on a tilted 3D plane. A rail of cards flicked sideways across a tilted plane. The cards do not crawl past on a loop — they are flicked: the rail leaves at speed, decelerates for well over a second and comes to rest about a card further along, the way a carousel behaves under a thumb rather than under a timer. The plane is not flat to the camera either. Measured on a recording's card edges, the horizontal scale grows 0.000825 per pixel of height abo

name: channel-thread
title: Channel Thread
desc: Slack-style chat animation: team messages arrive with typing dots. A work chat filling itself in, the way the channel actually reads: an avatar, a name in bold, a quiet timestamp and the messages as plain lines under them. Messages land one at a time, a second message from the same person joins the group without repeating the name, and when somebody new starts typing three dots hold their line until the words arrive. The transcript never creeps — it sits perfectly still between arrivals and then

name: check-cycle
title: Check Cycle
desc: Rotating words beside a checkbox: a sentence that finishes itself several ways. "Create your own" sits left of a ticked shadcn-style checkbox and the word to its right rolls up out of a slot — Intros, Demos, Launches, Changelogs, Tutorials, And more — then the line steps back a little and rests. Every number came off a recording, frame by frame: the two words in the slot move as one strip on the in-out cubic over exactly half a second, a roll every twenty frames. The type moves by fractions of a

name: click-type
title: Click Type
desc: Click to type: a prompt composer (Prompt Send's glass panel, writing surface and round send button) whose placeholder writes itself while a cursor flies in from the edge and clicks the field, then a hard cut into the field where the real prompt types at the caret and send arms. Two shots of one composer under a constant camera, anchored on the first letter, so the type never scales while it moves. Built on cursor-track.

name: count-grid
title: Count Grid
desc: Number count-up grid: cards multiply and a counter jumps, the it-scales stat shot. A grid of cards rushes in under a horizontal smear, settles on five and a label, then the camera pulls back a fraction while every empty cell around them fills in from the middle out and the number jumps. The "and it scales" shot, without a cut — one card is deliberately late to land, which is what makes the entry read as five separate things arriving rather than one picture being pushed in.

name: cursor-track
title: Cursor Track
desc: Cursor click animation: a mouse pointer that moves and clicks over any UI. A synthetic cursor that walks a path of normalized waypoints over any children and pulses a click ring on arrival. A hand-drawn macOS-style arrow with an outline that keeps it readable over arbitrary footage, or a touch puck — for UI sims, and for recordings whose real cursor never made it into the file.

name: cut-lockup
title: Cut Lockup
desc: Logo reveal in hard cuts. The logo lands huge on grid paper, steps down in three cuts, pushes in, cuts to night where its construction lines and anchor points draw themselves, then a paper panel wipes up onto the resting lockup. Cuts, scales, push and wipe are measured frame by frame off a reference recording.

name: dot-bloom
title: Dot Bloom
desc: Halftone dot transition. White dots spark over the outgoing shot while it washes out to cream, then the cream breaks into warm coral, peach and blush dots in drifting diagonal bands that thin out cell by cell until the incoming shot is all that is left. Every cell of every step is replayed from a reference recording.

name: drop-line
title: Drop Line
desc: Words cut past one card at a time, then the last word sinks out from under the dot of its own i

name: follower-rush
title: Follower Rush
desc: Follower count animation: X/Twitter follower notification with a count-up and avatar wave, for social proof. An X-style follower notification that piles up — avatars stack in and the count explodes, then the row bends into an undulating wave of faces.

name: font-shuffle
title: Font Shuffle
desc: Launch title animation: the line decodes out of scrambled glyphs set in the wrong typeface, flashes the accent, settles to ink, then the product name cycles through eleven typefaces (mono, light, humanist, pixel, script, slab, condensed, italic, blackletter, wide, bold grotesk) while the line zooms a step closer on each swap. Every beat is a held state measured off a recording frame by frame — timing, masks, layout, zoom and colour.

name: gather-lockup
title: Gather Lockup
desc: Logo reveal in two and a half seconds. A wall of your work sits under a line of type. The line falls apart word by word, the wall cuts in to a row of four, and each slot swaps its picture and hands over to your mark and wordmark. Measured frame by frame off a reference recording.

name: hello-zoom
title: Hello Zoom
desc: Words flicker in place, one line types on, then the camera dives through its own letters into the next card

name: hero-launch
title: Product Hero
desc: Product launch hero scene for a SaaS launch video intro. Cinematic product-launch hero — two cards slide into formation as the headline reveals above.

name: karaoke-captions
title: Karaoke Captions
desc: Karaoke captions: word-by-word highlighted subtitles synced to speech. A caption line that fills word by word as it is spoken — heavy outlined type that reads on any footage. Three presets: karaoke, highlight (the word rides an accent bar), clean.

name: laptop-frame
title: Laptop Frame
desc: MacBook laptop mockup animation that opens and zooms into your screenshot or video. MacBook-style laptop that opens, runs a dynamic-island notch notification, then dives the camera into the screen until an image or video fills the frame.

name: logo-assemble
title: Logo Assemble
desc: Logo reveal animation: image cards orbit and collapse into your logo and brand name. A single ring of image cards revolves around a centred title, then spins inward and drains to the middle — giving birth to a simple logo that slides left as the brand name reveals to its right.

name: logo-collapse
title: Logo Collapse
desc: Logo reveal intro: a stack of photos flicks through and collapses into your logo. A stack of shots flicked through, collapsing into your mark, and the wordmark landing beside it. One card holds the middle of the frame and cuts to the next shot, each smaller and each held for less time than the last, so the sequence winds itself up instead of running at a constant clip. Nothing cross-fades and nothing tweens between shots — the reference holds each card at a fixed size for its whole beat and then

name: logo-drift
title: Logo Drift
desc: Logo wall animation: a logo cloud of integrations drifting behind a headline. A field of tiles drifting past a headline while the camera pulls steadily back, so the wall of things-it-works-with keeps arriving from every edge. The pull-back is one linear scale measured at 0.176 per second across every tile; the words do not fade in, they arrive 1.216× large and 4.3px soft and land in 140ms.

name: logo-flicker
title: Logo Flicker
desc: Logo reveal intro: a fast image flicker that settles on your logo. Images flip across a central card very fast, the flicker decelerates and fades, and the logo and brand name resolve underneath — a strobe of imagery settling onto the mark.

name: moodboard-reveal
title: Moodboard Reveal
desc: Photo gallery reveal: a moodboard fly-through that lands on a hero image. A kinetic headline with a swapping inline image, then a scattered gallery of photos flies in, the camera pushes through it as the background lifts from near-black to off-white, and it lands on a single hero image.

name: orb-swarm
title: Orb Swarm
desc: Kinetic typography scene with glass orbs: a sentence told one beat at a time while four orbs burst out of it, split into eight and sixteen, wind into a clockwise vortex, collapse into a knot, pay out as a chain, loop around the closing words and shrink away bead by bead. Every phase was measured frame by frame off a 24fps reference and is replayed on the same clock; the orbs are shaded per pixel into a canvas (a scrolling band texture bowed like latitude lines, a soft glass edge) and the type is

name: orbit-gallery
title: Orbit Gallery
desc: Image gallery intro: photos spiral into the centre around a title. An image-universe hero: a continuous stream of photos flows along an Archimedean spiral (a vortex) from the frame edges into the center — evenly spaced by arc length, shrinking and rotating to follow the coil, with the title held in the clear middle. A slow, cinematic opener for launch and editorial videos.

name: phone-frame
title: Phone Frame
desc: iPhone mockup animation: phone device frame for app screenshots and screen recordings. iPhone-style device frame with a dynamic island and a screen slot — flat or lightly 3D-tilted, with rise, rotate-in, or float entrances and a subtle float loop.

name: phone-stack
title: Phone Stack
desc: Stacked phone screens with video. Phone screens rise out of a blur from below one after another, and each new one pushes the stack back: the older screens shrink and step up so only their tops peek out above the newest. Every screen plays its own clip under an iOS status bar. Proportions measured off a reference recording.

name: portal-intro
title: Portal Intro
desc: Sentence-to-picture intro. The lead words fade up one at a time, the line re-sets with a small rounded picture chip inside it and leans in until the chip takes the frame; a title types itself over the picture, lifts away, and the mark and the name arrive. Fitted frame by frame from a reference recording.

name: prompt-send
title: Prompt Send
desc: AI prompt typing animation: a chat input types a prompt and a cursor clicks send. A composer that unrolls from a hairline, writes a brief into itself while the camera cuts in and rides the caret, then cuts back out to the send button as a pointer arrives and clicks it. The typing is eased, not constant — 17 chars/sec on the first word, 33 in the middle, a settle on the last three. Long copy scrolls the field under its own caret and extra suggestions wrap, so the panel fits whatever you put in it

name: prompt-zoom
title: Prompt Zoom
desc: AI prompt zoom: an assistant home screen that cuts into the chat input as the prompt types. An assistant landing screen that offers its suggestions, then cuts — hard, in a single frame — into the caret, where the prompt types itself. The push-in is a measured 2.547× anchored on the text insertion point, not an animated zoom.

name: pulsing-border
title: Pulsing Border
desc: AI glow border: a pulsing thinking frame around the screen. Glowing 'AI is working' frame — a soft pulsing border overlay that breathes around the scene edges while a response streams.

name: punch-lines
title: Punch Lines
desc: Kinetic typography title cards: bold statements that cut hard between beats. A run of full-frame title cards that cut hard between beats. A statement card is flicked in from the left line by line and settles on a critically damped curve, then rushes past the camera; a hero card punches its words up from a third of their size in a wave and pushes slowly forward until it cuts. Every curve is fitted from frame measurements — the slide to 0.42px rms over 37 frames.

name: reel-collage
title: Reel Collage
desc: Photo reel that shuts into a collage. A picture cuts through a quick reel between two captions and slowly zooms, then shuts like an eyelid while the captions fold into one stacked line; the copy swaps, the lines split, and a scattered collage blooms in around them on a peach flush. Every curve is fitted from a reference recording, frame by frame.

name: reel-wall
title: Reel Wall
desc: Curved video wall for Remotion. A ring of vertical clips turns past in the dark: it eases in from rest on twos, then keeps turning at an even speed. The ring, lens and ease are fitted frame by frame from a reference recording.

name: roster-grant
title: Roster Grant
desc: Access granted animation: a cursor clicks a CTA and team avatars switch on. Three rows of roster cards stream past a call to action, a pointer walks in and clicks it, and the monograms start turning to the accent one every seven frames — top row, middle, bottom, top, bottom, middle, so it reads as a system granting rather than a list iterating. The camera and the middle row's clearance around the pill settle on the same measured exponential; the outer rows deliberately do not, which is what stop

name: screen-recording
title: Screen Recording
desc: Screen recording zoom: crop and auto-zoom a product demo capture. The treatment that turns a raw screen capture into a shot: crop the browser and OS chrome off each edge as a fraction, fit what is left to the frame, and run a keyframed camera that pushes in on whatever matters at a given frame and holds until the next move. Takes a video or a still through the same track.

name: search-typing
title: Search Typing
desc: Search bar typing animation for AI search and command palette demos. A search field wider than the shot: two thirds in frame, then it comes forward, types across its left half, pages to its right half, and goes back. Every proportion is measured, and the scale pivots on the text baseline so the type never climbs the pixel grid.

name: sky-lockup
title: Sky Lockup
desc: Logo outro in under two seconds. A one-line promise takes itself apart word by word, the white page washes off to a soft sky, and the mark in the middle of the sentence slides over, turns white and picks up your wordmark. Measured frame by frame off a reference recording.

name: spec-sweep
title: Spec Sweep
desc: A one-line spec slides in word by word while a highlight runs along it and an icon charges up

name: status-cycle
title: Status Cycle
desc: Status badge animation: a pill whose label cycles through states. A centred line whose status pill cycles: the label rolls up behind a hard clip while the pill's width springs past its target and back, and the line re-centres around it. The field then crossfades and a column of chips steps up from below. Copy, palette and every timing are props; the curves are fitted from frame measurements, not eyeballed.

name: terminal-simulator
title: Terminal Simulator
desc: Terminal animation: CLI demo that types commands and prints output. Terminal window with chunked command playback, freeze-frame pauses, step scrolling, and an optional cursor-pinned zoom camera.

name: text-build
title: Text Build
desc: Word-by-word text build animation that keeps the line centred. Words enter one at a time while already-placed words physically reflow to stay centered — a growing line on the x axis or a growing stack on the y axis.

name: text-highlight
title: Text Highlight
desc: Text highlight animation: marker highlighter, underline, strikethrough and shimmer on a word. Animated emphasis on one span inside a static sentence — marker sweep, color shift, underline, strikethrough-replace, or shimmer.

name: text-reveal
title: Text Reveal
desc: Text reveal animation: word-by-word and letter-by-letter kinetic typography with blur-in, fade, slide, scale and tracking-in presets. One staggered enter/exit text animator: fade, slide, blur, scale, mask and tracking effects over character, word, line or block units, with 14 classic looks as presets.

name: text-rewrite
title: Text Rewrite
desc: Text rewrite animation, a typewriter line that deletes and retypes its ending. A line that writes itself a word at a time, comes forward and gets selected — then its opening is swept away by a clip that cuts letters in half as it passes, and a new ending is written on while the line slides to its new centre. The mark rides the sweeping edge throughout.

name: text-select
title: Text Select
desc: Typewriter with text selection: a line types word by word, then gets highlighted. A line that writes itself a word at a time — each one arriving in the accent and cooling to the foreground a beat later, so exactly one word is ever coloured — then pushes forward to full size on a baseline-pivoted scale and gets selected, the drag sweeping across under a gradient sheen with a hard caret edge.

name: text-swap
title: Text Swap
desc: Text swap animation, rotating headline that replaces one line with another. Replaces one line of text with another using exit-then-enter scheduling, with five transition presets: fade-through, crossfade, shared-axis-y, shared-axis-z, and cut.

name: text-swell
title: Text Swell
desc: Kinetic typography title with a bouncing letter wave. A title reveal where the lead word floats toward the viewer and hangs there while the sentence assembles around it — each trailing word pushes in and its letters bounce up off the baseline in a wave — before the whole line falls back to size.

name: title-sweep
title: Title Sweep
desc: An end title lit by a gradient that travels through the letters, cuts in the dark, and a second title takes over

name: type-morph
title: Type Morph
desc: Typewriter effect: a headline types with a blinking caret, then morphs letter by letter. A headline that types itself under a glowing caret, sheds its lead, morphs letter by letter, and ends under a colour flood.

name: word-captions
title: Word Captions
desc: TikTok-style captions: animated subtitles with word pop, Hormozi and MrBeast styles for Reels and Shorts. Burned-in captions in the styles big channels actually use — heavy Montserrat, a real outside outline so they read on any footage, and the spoken word springing to an accent. Four presets: beast, hormozi, pop, clean.

name: word-flip
title: Word Flip
desc: Word flip text rotator: a typewriter headline with a 3D rotating word. A headline types itself out, then one word cycles on a 3D flip — it sinks into an anticipation dip, throws up and away about its baseline under motion blur, and the next word unfurls from below. The slot is reserved from the first keystroke, so nothing in the sentence ever reflows.

name: word-gather
title: Word Gather
desc: Word-by-word sentence animation: words fly in out of order and settle into the line. A sentence that arrives one word at a time, out of order, and gathers. The first word holds the middle of the frame on its own; then the rest drop in around it — not in reading order and not where they belong — each landing near its slot in the accent colour and sliding the last of the way home, turning to ink as it settles. The line makes room for them as they come, and when the last one is down the whole block

name: word-wheel
title: Word Wheel
desc: Rotating words text: a slot machine word wheel that spins and stops on one word. A column of words that spins like a reel and stops on one of them. A fixed lead-in holds the left of the line and the word that finishes the sentence lives in a slot beside it — one row of a taller column whose other words are visible above and below, smaller and grey, fading out toward the top and bottom of the frame. The reel rolls, decelerates over a second and three quarters and comes to rest with one word at fu

name: wordmark-cut
title: Wordmark Cut
desc: Wordmark reveal end card: a huge brand name with a hard cut to a close-up. A wordmark twice the width of the frame, cooling from a lit gradient to ink while it settles, and then a hard cut onto its last letters and the dot — 1.71× nearer, with a shallow depth of field the wide shot does not have, which is the only thing that says the second shot is closer rather than just bigger. It holds a beat and pushes in, still accelerating on the last frame.
